letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking practices on kingfisher.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking practices observed on https://kingfisher.com during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 04:12 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited the site, clicked the cookie banner option “Decline cookies”, then browsed the pages listed below and recorded what was still sent.

Pages visited after rejection were:
1. https://www.kingfisher.com/franchise-and-partnerships
2. https://www.kingfisher.com/our-banners-and-brands
3. https://www.kingfisher.com/investors

The privacy policy reviewed was: https://www.kingfisher.com/privacy-policy

The points I would like you to explain are:
1. Our review suggests tracking continued after the visitor clicked “Decline cookies”. Google requests continued and YouTube tracking cookies were present or set. This appears inconsistent with the policy statement that users can turn other companies’ cookies on or off.
2. Before any choice was made on the cookie banner, 5 Google tracking cookies were already set: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID. VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID held what looked like unique identifiers.
3. After cookies were rejected, 35 requests were still sent to google-analytics.com, googletagmanager.com and youtube.com.
4. The privacy policy names 4 companies, but the audit saw Google and found no mention of it. I appreciate the policy may describe some recipients only by category.
5. Our review suggests the observed YouTube-set Google cookies are not identified in the cookie list. Several Google cookie names were found, but the policy does not appear to identify those YouTube cookie names or explain their purposes and expiry periods.

Please would you:
1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking technologies from being set or used without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
